title: Robotics and the future of on-orbit labor
summary: SpaceNews interviews Icarus Robotics CEO Ethan Barajas at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference about the role of robotics in future on-orbit labor. The discussion highlights advancements and applications in space robotics.

title: Aerospace demonstrates DiskSats in low-Earth orbit
summary: Aerospace Corp. is demonstrating the viability of DiskSats, pancake-shaped satellites, in low-Earth orbit following their launch on a Rocket Lab Electron in December. The initiative aims to showcase the potential of this novel satellite design.

title: Spirit Electronics Adds Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology Space Grade Components to Online Store Ahead of SmallSat 2026
summary: Spirit Electronics has added space-grade components from Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology to its online store ahead of SmallSat 2026. This move expands the availability of high-reliability electronics for space applications.

title: The Fuel for the Next Generation of Cislunar Exploration? Technology and Talent.
summary: The article discusses the future of cislunar exploration, emphasizing the role of technology and talent in advancing space missions beyond Earth's orbit. It highlights the long-term benefits of lunar exploration, including scientific discoveries and national security advantages.

title: Tory Bruno Named Honorary Chair Of World Space Week 2027
summary: Tory Bruno, President of National Security at Blue Origin, has been named Honorary Chair of World Space Week 2027. The World Space Week Association made the announcement highlighting his contributions to the space industry.

title: New Novaspace forecast: 6,500+ EO satellites to launch by 2035
summary: Novaspace predicts over 6,500 Earth observation (EO) satellites will launch by 2035, generating $155.9 billion in manufacturing revenues. The expansion is driven by governments increasing sovereign intelligence and surveillance capabilities.

title: Moog Highlights Huntsville Expansion and New Hardware-in-the-Loop Lab During Space and Missile Defense Symposium
summary: Moog Inc. announced a major expansion of its Huntsville, AL facility, including a new secure Hypersonic/Interceptor Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) lab. The announcement was made during the Space and Missile Defense Symposium.

title: Rock West Composites® Is Premiering Its New STRATOPultrusion™ Product Line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference
summary: Rock West Composites is showcasing its new space-grade STRATOPultrusion™ product line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference in Salt Lake City. The event highlights advancements in satellite technology and materials.

title: Pluto losing its planet status may be the best thing that ever happened to solar system diversity
summary: Pluto's reclassification as a dwarf planet has enhanced our understanding of solar system diversity. The change has been beneficial for both scientific progress and Pluto itself.

summary: The article discusses the 25th anniversary of the film 'Ghosts of Mars' and examines the feasibility of terraforming Mars for human habitation. Experts weigh in on whether the sci-fi vision is becoming closer to reality.

title: 'Project Hail Mary' and 'The Martian' author Andy Weir is headed back to outer space, but not how you'd expect
summary: Andy Weir, author of 'Project Hail Mary' and 'The Martian,' will executive produce a new Audible sci-fi drama titled 'Exoplanet' set to release this fall. This marks his return to space-themed storytelling in a non-traditional format.

title: Goodbye, Falcon 9: SpaceX planning to retire workhorse launcher when Starship is up and running
summary: SpaceX plans to retire its Falcon 9 rocket once the Starship megarocket becomes operational. This shift could significantly impact the current launch market dominated by Falcon 9.

summary: SpaceX is set to achieve a rocket-reuse record during its 100th Falcon 9 launch of the year on August 25. The event will be livestreamed.

title: Why do we care so much that Pluto isn't a planet?
summary: Twenty years after Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet, the debate over its planetary status continues to spark strong opinions. Experts discuss why the controversy remains emotionally charged for many.

title: Is the Perseid meteor shower going to get even more spectacular? Jupiter could send more 'shooting stars' towards Earth in 2028
summary: Jupiter's gravity may enhance the 2028 Perseid meteor shower, potentially making it more spectacular. The planet could trigger an outburst of 'shooting stars' during the shower's peak.

title: At 25% off, this beginner-friendly Celestron telescope will bring the lunar eclipse closer
summary: A Celestron telescope is being offered at a 25% discount at Walmart, making it ideal for viewing the lunar eclipse and Saturn. The PowerSeeker 80EQ model is beginner-friendly and nearly 50% off.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 24, 2006: Pluto loses its planet status
summary: On August 24, 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet, stripping it of its planetary status. This decision was made during the IAU's general assembly.

title: Satellite sees Greenland's most significant floating ice loss in over a decade | Space photo of the day for Aug. 24, 2026
summary: A satellite captured Greenland's most significant floating ice loss in over a decade, showing a fractured 'ice tongue' in the imagery. This marks a concerning trend in polar ice decline.

summary: Falcon Heavy is set to launch the Roman Space Telescope, while Falcon 9 will deploy Starlink satellites. The week will also feature five additional orbital launches from China, the U.S., and French Guiana.

summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch, scheduled for August 30, after reaching final integration and rehearsal milestones.

summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket toppled after achieving a significant milestone with a successful landing. This marks a key advancement for China's commercial spaceflight sector.

summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14. Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine assembly for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch around 2026. This comes as the company advances its fully reusable vehicle development amid high-profile competition.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, completed its second flight with a successful first-stage landing, marking a significant milestone for the company.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location near Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 mission following the recent failure of the Chang Zheng 7A rocket. The upcoming week also includes multiple launches, including Starlink missions.

summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing development of its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also promoting its Alpha rocket. The company is making progress on multiple fronts, including its Eclipse program.

summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration.

summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return. The project aims to advance reusable space transportation capabilities in Europe.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3, a mission by the European Space Agency (ESA), will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to observe the Sun's outer atmosphere with unprecedented precision.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise alignment capabilities.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This approach allows scientists to gather more data than during a brief natural eclipse.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, a deep space asteroid mission. This offers a unique opportunity to test software millions of kilometers from Earth.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying by using a coronagraph to block the Sun's glare and observe the solar corona, while also capturing images of Earth. The mission aims to test precise satellite positioning for future space science and exploration.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together startups and space industry leaders to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities.

title: Beyond Reach Labs Unveils Flarewing Deployable Solar Arrays
summary: Beyond Reach Labs has introduced Flarewing, a patent-pending deployable solar array system designed to fold flat during launch. This technology aims to optimize space-based solar power generation.

summary: Starcloud has raised a $250 million extension to its Series A funding round, bringing the total valuation to $2.3 billion.

title: Letara Raises ¥2.6B to Build its Hybrid Rocket Engine Tech
summary: Japanese propulsion startup Letara raised ¥2.6 billion ($16 million) in a pre-Series A funding round to develop its low-cost hybrid rocket engine technology.

title: SpaceWERX Announces 2026 STRATFI Awardees
summary: Space Force announced the newest awardees of the SpaceWERX Strategic Funding Increase program during the Fed Supernova conference. The awards were revealed at the event.

summary: The White House, through the Office of Science and Technology Policy, released a new National Security Science & Technology Strategy. This strategy aims to guide national security efforts through scientific and technological advancements.

summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial nuclear mission to the Moon, partnering with Firefly Aerospace to send a radioisotope heating unit on a 2028 mission. The demonstration aims to showcase Zeno's capability to provide 5W of power for lunar operations.

summary: NanoAvionics has upgraded its MP42 satellite bus line with a new 500 kg platform, making it the company's largest offering. The upgrade expands the capabilities of the MP42 line for larger satellite missions.

summary: Kepler Communications has launched service on its new optical data relay constellation for commercial and government customers. The service became active following a SpaceX launch.

title: KSAT Rolls Out Demonstration Campaign for Hyper Hybrid RF/Optional Network
summary: KSAT has launched a demonstration campaign for its Hyperion Hyper hybrid RF/optical relay network. The campaign aims to showcase the capabilities of the next-generation network.

summary: The Space Development Agency (SDA) reports that on-orbit checkouts for its Tranche 1 satellites, launched in July, are advancing faster than expected after an initial slow start. SDA Director Dr. Gurpartap highlighted the progress during a recent update.

title: Fireside Chat with German Space Command: Featuring Major General Michael Traut
summary: A fireside chat featured Major General Michael Traut, Commander of the German Space Command, discussing Germany's military space operations and efforts to protect space assets. The event highlighted the integration of space capabilities into national defense strategies.

title: White House Targets Support for 1,000 Launches Per Year by 2030
summary: The White House announced a goal to support over 1,000 space launches and reentries annually by 2030 through a new National Security Presidential Memorandum. This initiative aims to bolster U.S. space industry capabilities and national security.

title: The Evolution of the Space Edge With Voyager CTO Paul Tilghman
summary: The article discusses the evolution of spaceborne computing, focusing on the shift to the 'space edge' rather than orbital data centers. It features insights from Voyager Space's CTO, Paul Tilghman.

title: Starcloud Adds $250M to Series A at a $2.3B Valuation
summary: Orbital data center startup Starcloud raised an additional $250 million for its Series A round, increasing its valuation to $2.3 billion just five months after the initial raise. The round was led by Manhattan West.

title: Space Norway Appoints Rune Jensen as Acting CEO With Morten Tengs Departure
summary: Space Norway appointed Rune Jensen as acting CEO following the departure of Morten Tengs, who will step down at the end of August. The company will now search for a permanent CEO.

title: Sypris Electronics Wins Manufacturing Deal to Support LEO Constellation
summary: Sypris Electronics has secured a manufacturing contract to produce power processing units for an unnamed Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. The deal marks a significant step in supporting next-generation satellite infrastructure.
